headline: ARMY DETONATES
dek: The nation's entire stockpile, about 5 tons, was blown up Wednesday morning at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, AP reports.

nodes.text: The 8th Circuit denies environmental groups' emergency stay and lifts its pause on the EPA permit.
Gov. Reynolds declares a disaster emergency in Des Moines, Lee and Van Buren counties. A FEMA alert tells people 5 to 20 miles away to stay indoors.
The Army detonates the degraded lead azide. A plume is observed.
The EPA keeps testing air, soil and water. Evacuated residents get a call when it's all clear, the Army said.

means.label: Why now:
means.text: Officials said the degraded material risked exploding on its own as temperatures dropped.

means.label: Before the blast:
means.text: The EPA said it collected more than 1,200 samples and detected no lead in the air.

means.label: The concerns:
means.text: Environmentalists raised possible health and environmental effects from lead dust.

sources: Sources: AP, Nov. 25 (story and live updates); EPA; U.S. Army; 8th Circuit order, Nov. 23; Iowa governor's office and WQAD, Nov. 24.
